title: Mapping the Sensory & Motor Homunculi and Cortical Magnification
description: Chart two-point tactile discrimination thresholds across the body and correlate findings with Penfield's cortical homunculus.
problemStatement:
In a human psychophysics laboratory, researchers measure the **Two-Point Discrimination Threshold** (the minimal distance between two caliper points where a participant perceives two separate touches rather than one) across five body locations:
1. Index fingertip
2. Upper lip
3. Forearm
4. Middle of the back
5. Big toe

### Your Mission:
1. **Data Prediction**: Rank these five sites from smallest discrimination threshold (highest tactile acuity, ~2-3 mm) to largest threshold (lowest tactile acuity, ~40-50 mm).
2. **Receptive Field Physiology**: Explain how receptor density and receptive field size in Merkel discs and Meissner corpuscles account for these differences.
3. **Homunculus Correlation**: Relate these physical findings directly to the proportional surface area of Primary Somatosensory Cortex (S1) dedicated to each body part (cortical magnification).
hints: Hint 1: Fingertips and lips have tiny, densely packed receptive fields that map to huge cortical areas in S1.
Hint 2: The back has large, overlapping receptive fields with very sparse cortical representation.
